text:
maria: Quick sync — I’m putting together a canonical benchmark for mixed-precision quant runs (FP8 / INT8 / 4-bit). We need to lock the warmup strategy, power cap policy, tokenization seeds, KV-cache behavior, and what kernel-selection signals we record. Any strong opinions?

jin: +1 on a canonical plan. My suggestions: 1) warmup = 3 modes: short prefix (32 tokens), full-context fill (up to seq len), and empty-KV cold run. We should run each mode separately. 2) deterministic tokenization seeds for each prompt (documented).

alex: For kernel selection metrics: record per-op latency (ms), kernel name, batch size, seq len, kv-hit-rate, and CPU spin time. Also log GPU power telemetry (DCGM) and SM utilization. We should snapshot chosen kernel + rationale (why chooser picked it).
dana: Calibration impacts both perf and quality. We need to store calibration artifacts (scale vectors, histograms) and link them to runs. Evaluate quality with a small holdout set: perplexity + embedding-sim + a human-like prompt pass/fail. If quantization causes >0.5% emb-sim drop or >1pt perplexity regression, flag.
sara: Batching heuristics: include continuous batching enabled/disabled, max batch size, batching timeout, and concurrency level. Measure p50/p90/p95/p99 latency and per-token throughput. Capture queue length distribution. :chart_with_upwards_trend:
mike: We saw an INT8 attention kernel regression yesterday where token gen p99 jumped 20ms on long seqs. Need to include regression-diff artifacts and a golden-run comparison (bit-identical where possible, or seeded gen).
bench-bot: nightly-quant-1977774444-run: artifacts uploaded -> s3://redwood-bench/quant/1977774444/ (profiles, nvprof, dcgm.csv, calib/*.json) :white_check_mark:
jin: KV cache behavior: two axes — prefix reuse (same prompt repeated) vs incremental streaming. For streaming, measure KV churn cost (how often we reallocate/reorder caches). Add a small microbenchmark that repeatedly appends tokens and measures amortized token cost.
alex: Profiling: capture kernel-level timelines (ns), kernel occupancy, and memory copies. Include traces with timestamps aligned to request IDs so we can correlate chooser decisions to tails. Also capture host->device queueing delays.
dana: On calibration: run both global per-layer and per-channel calibrations. Keep calibration budget fixed (N samples) across quant types for fair comparison. Document the dataset used for calib (sampled tokens, tokenization script).
sara: Fair comparisons: 1) identical prompt corpus (seeded), 2) same power cap policy (e.g., 250W vs 300W tests), 3) run each config N times (N>=5) shuffled order to avoid thermal bias, 4) clear caches between runs for cold-run mode.
mike: Also log software stack: cuda/cuDNN/llc versions, compiler flags, kernel chooser commit hash. Those changed and caused surprises before.
maria: Good notes. Proposed minimal artifacts for each run: - run config json (batching, power cap, kernels allowed, warmup mode) - calibration artifacts - perf trace (timeline + nvml/dcgm) - summaries (p50/p90/p95/p99, tok/s, gpu-pct) - quality diffs vs float32 baseline - kernel-chooser logs. Store under s3://redwood-bench/quant/<ts>/<config>/

Action items:
- alex -> add kernel chooser log schema and exporter (due EOD)
- jin -> implement 3 warmup modes and add cold-warm streaming microbench (tomorrow)
- dana -> define calibration dataset + quality gating thresholds (this week)
- sara -> add batching telemetry hooks (queue histograms + latency buckets)
- mike -> reproduce INT8 regression with the canonical script and upload artifacts

maria: If nobody objects, I’ll make the canonical script and kick off a smoke sweep across FP8/INT8/4bit tomorrow morning. We’ll gate CI on the quality thresholds once dana finalizes them. :eyes:
